summary: Bunzai protects the local library, provider credentials, API authority and machine resources across separate trust boundaries. Imported scripts remain data until explicitly invoked through supported execution gates. The overview links each detailed boundary to its authoritative reference rather than repeating changing numeric limits. Archives have selection and decompression checks; regex has conservative validation, construction bounds and isolated imported execution; markup and Lua have separate rendering and capability controls. Local API authority is distinct from opt-in remote access. Provider requests send selected conversation and observations to the configured host, with redirect checks on guarded HTTP paths; external CLIs and connected processes have separate network authority. Damaged vault reads reject instead of becoming empty state, and the keychain diagnostic uses a private invocation namespace. Source tests, native platform evidence and packaged-host evidence are distinguished. Packaged WebView2 isolation, native regex preemption, weaker local key-file protection, missing passphrase UI and unchanged vault cache/concurrency behavior remain explicit limits.

sections.title: Trust boundaries
sections.summary: Untrusted files, archives, markup, Lua, regex, model responses and remote requests meet different gates. Import and conversion do not execute imported scripts; enabling an imported regex set is an invocation rather than an import effect. The primary Studio listener is loopback, while remote access is an explicit separate authority. Provider-backed turns send selected conversation and observations to the chosen provider. The boundary table directs readers to the owners for canonical conversion and semantic fidelity, archive checks and residuals, conservative regex validation and native-call limits, sanitized rendering, capability-restricted Lua, local Host/Origin/bearer checks, remote join/device controls, encrypted credential storage and per-hop provider egress. This is a navigation overview, not an independently maintained set of detailed limits or a claim that every boundary is proven in a packaged host.

sections.title: Evidence and remaining limits
sections.summary: Code-level tests do not establish real OS-keychain or packaged WebView behavior. The second sandbox origin has HTTP-layer tests but its packaged storage and credentialed API separation remain unmeasured; same-origin fallback is degraded. Native synchronous regex calls cannot be interrupted mid-match, so static refusal and construction bounds reduce risk without proving a deadline. The local identity-file fallback is weaker than OS key storage and there is no settings-driven passphrase unlock. Missing vaults read empty, while other read/envelope/plaintext failures refuse later saves; the narrow damaged-identity recovery preserves originals and reports the incident. Cache lifecycle and cross-process write-conflict safety are unchanged. The keychain probe uses a fresh service and cleans only its own entries, with isolated regressions for credential preservation and failed cleanup. Native-platform proof still requires recorded platform results.
